role: The trapdoor (id 96): a thin slab against one wall face, opened and closed by right click or redstone (bit 4), which also flips which face it hangs from; drops itself when its wall goes away.

members.name: BlockTrapDoor
members.note: id 96: Material.wood row, full-cube static bounds (the real bounds are per state)

members.name: getBlocksMovement
members.note: an open trapdoor (bit 4) is passable for pathfinding and movement

members.name: getSelectedBoundingBoxFromPool
members.note: The state bounds (open, top, facing); idx-blocks-s1 places a trapdoor on a wall and toggles it through the pick; render-only: every caller is the client renderer (RenderBlocks, RenderItem, ItemRenderer, RenderGlobal's outline, the item icon and colour hooks); row recordings draw no frames

members.name: getCollisionBoundingBoxFromPool
members.note: case 96: the closed 0.1875 slab, or the open door's side slab (bit-4 doors report only the side box)

members.name: setBlockBoundsForItemRender
members.note: The item form (the 3/16 slab) in block_item_model.c; the block-icon goldens draw it; render-only: every caller is the client renderer (RenderBlocks, RenderItem, ItemRenderer, RenderGlobal's outline, the item icon and colour hooks); row recordings draw no frames

members.name: onBlockActivated
members.note: case ID_TRAPDOOR: toggles bit 4 (the iron material's early return only matters for iron trapdoors, which 1.7.10 has no item for); the client half (the toggle on WorldClient before the same tick's move, the 1003 sound's Math.random and world rand draws) is survival.c:client_toggle_openable

members.name: onNeighborBlockChange
members.note: drops itself when the block behind its facing is gone, then the redstone toggle

members.name: onBlockPlaced
members.note: the facing meta 0..3 plus the top-hung bit 8 from the hit Y

members.name: func_150118_d
members.note: The open bit (meta & 4) read inline where it matters (collision, pathing, activation).

members.name: func_150119_a
members.note: an opaque full cube, glowstone, a slab or a stair can hold a trapdoor; place.c has its own copy of the same test

notes: blockcb.c's header notes the conversion-path neighbor notifications that can pop a trapdoor; test_place.c covers placement and test_activate.c the toggle. lane/idxblocks: idx-blocks-s1 places a trapdoor on a wall (top half) and opens and closes it.
